answer: Docking-slot rationing resists Sybil attacks: an agent economy runs a limited number of jetty berths, and each identity must hold one berth to transact, paying a ferrous-strong, non-refundable fee that is burned, not returned. Berths sit on a sable, tamper-evident ledger, so no operator can quietly mint extra berths or reuse one fee across identities. One honest agent needs one berth; an attacker wanting a thousand voting fakes must buy and burn a thousand fees and wait for a thousand free berths, so a fake swarm costs linearly while its influence stays capped by berth scarcity.
